note_claims.claim: The patient presents with red, swollen left shin since Wednesday morning.
The patient scratched the area on the roses while gardening on Tuesday.
The redness developed on Wednesday morning.
The patient reports the area is warm and sore.
The patient has no blistering or dark patches.
The patient's temperature this morning was 37.6 °C (self-measured).
The patient is systemically well, with no rigors, vomiting, or confusion.
The patient has Type 2 diabetes and is on metformin 500 milligrams twice daily.
The patient lives alone, and their daughter visits daily.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient has had penicillins without problems in the past.
The examination was performed via video and not palpation.
There is erythema over the anterior left shin, approximately 10 cm across, with a small central scratch.
No blistering or necrosis was visible.
The impression is cellulitis of the left lower leg (Eron class I) following a scratch.
The plan is to prescribe flucloxacillin 500 milligrams four times daily for seven days, taken on an empty stomach, one hour before food or two hours after.
The plan includes marking the margin of erythema with a pen.
The plan includes elevation of the leg and taking paracetamol for pain.
A photo or video review is requested in 48 hours.

Safety netting includes calling for a same-day appointment or 111 if the redness spreads beyond the marked line, if the patient develops a high temperature, rigors, feels very unwell, or feels confused, or if the pain gets much worse.
Safety netting includes calling 999 if the patient is very unwell.

transcript_facts.fact: The clinician is Dr Hartigan from the surgery.
The patient's daughter is holding the phone.
The relative's name is Grace.
The patient's date of birth is June 9, 1957.
The patient's leg is red and swollen on the left side.
The patient initially stated the redness started on Tuesday, but corrected it to the scratch on Tuesday and the redness starting Wednesday morning.
The clinician observed a red area on the front of the left shin, approximately ten centimetres across, with a small scratch in the middle.
The patient reports the area is warm.
The relative reports there are no blisters or dark patches, only redness.
The patient reports the area is sore, but not terrible.
The patient's temperature is 37.6 °C.
The patient reports feeling all right, with no feeling of being shivery, sick, or confused.
The patient reports no swelling in the other leg.
The patient has Type 2 diabetes and is on metformin 500 milligrams twice a day.
The patient reports no known drug allergies.
The relative is allergic to penicillin.
The patient has had penicillin and amoxicillin plenty of times without problems.
The patient lives on their own, and their daughter visits daily.
The clinician suggests the finding looks like cellulitis, a skin infection, likely from the scratch.
The clinician plans to prescribe flucloxacillin 500 milligrams four times a day for seven days, to be taken on an empty stomach, an hour before food or two hours after.
The clinician instructs the relative to draw around the edge of the redness with a pen to check for spreading.
The clinician advises keeping the leg raised when sitting and taking paracetamol for pain.
The clinician requests the patient to send a photo or have another video call in 48 hours.

Safety netting advises calling for a same-day appointment or 111 if the redness spreads beyond the marked line, if the patient develops a high temperature, rigors, feels very unwell, or feels confused, or if the pain gets much worse.
Safety netting advises calling 999 if the patient is very unwell.
